section: Centre-State legislative relations - Articles 245-255, doctrine of repugnancy, parliamentary legislation on state list
subsections: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255
Doctrine of pith and substance applied to list conflicts - cases

accepted.s: Article 255 of the Constitution primarily relates to which of the following?
o: Repugnancy between Union and State laws
Recommendations and previous sanctions as matters of procedure
Establishment of additional courts
Residuary legislative powers
accepted.x: Article 255 provides that certain recommendations and previous sanctions are matters of procedure. Their absence does not necessarily invalidate an Act if the required assent is subsequently given.
accepted.tq: Use the article-number and subject association without confusing procedural requirements with substantive invalidity.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 246A, Parliament and the State Legislatures have power to make laws relating to which subject?
o: Goods and Services Tax
Additional courts
Residuary matters
Inter-State water disputes
accepted.x: Article 246A deals with the legislative power relating to Goods and Services Tax.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed Article 246 provisions and their distinct subjects.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is specifically authorised by Article 247?
o: The President may establish courts for State laws
The Governor may establish additional High Courts
The Supreme Court may create courts for local bodies
Parliament may establish additional courts for better administration of Union laws
accepted.x: Article 247 empowers Parliament to establish additional courts for the better administration of laws made by Parliament or existing laws relating to matters in the Union List.
accepted.tq: Ask who has the power and for what purpose; this avoids authority-swapping traps.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 248 deals with residuary legislative powers.
2. Article 252 enables Parliament to legislate for two or more States with their consent.
3. States adopting a law under Article 252 cannot subsequently adopt it if they were not original consenting States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A State that did not originally consent may subsequently adopt the parliamentary law under Article 252; therefore, statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect absolute statement concerning later adoption by other States.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the legislative effect of Article 253?
o: It applies only during a National Emergency
It permits States alone to implement international agreements
It permits Parliament to make laws implementing international agreements
It is confined to agreements concerning the Union List
accepted.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing treaties, agreements and conventions with foreign countries or decisions made at international conferences.
accepted.tq: Test the scope of parliamentary power by rejecting restrictive words such as 'only' and 'confined'.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A law made by Parliament under Article 249 or Article 250 is inconsistent with a law made by a State Legislature. Which law prevails during the relevant period?
o: The Parliamentary law under Article 251
The law made later by the Governor
The State law, because State subjects are exclusively protected
Both laws become void automatically
accepted.x: Article 251 deals with inconsistency between laws made under Articles 249 or 250 and State laws. The Parliamentary law prevails to the extent of inconsistency.
accepted.tq: Link the operative article on inconsistency with the exceptional source of parliamentary power.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Article 254 is correct?
o: A State law always prevails over a Union law in the Concurrent List
A Union law generally prevails over an inconsistent State law in the Concurrent field
Repugnancy applies only between Union List and State List laws
A State law assented to by the Chief Justice can prevail throughout India
accepted.x: Article 254 provides that Union law ordinarily prevails over an inconsistent State law in the Concurrent field. A State law reserved for and receiving the President's assent may prevail in that State.
accepted.tq: Use the field of operation and the assent exception to distinguish repugnancy from ordinary legislative conflict.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: An Act requiring the previous recommendation or sanction of the Governor or President has been passed without it, but the Governor or President subsequently gives assent. What is the constitutional consequence under Article 255?
o: The Act is not invalid merely for want of that recommendation or previous sanction
The Act is automatically void in all circumstances
The Act applies only to Union Territories
The Act becomes a constitutional amendment
accepted.x: Article 255 treats the requirement of recommendation or previous sanction as a matter of procedure. Subsequent assent prevents invalidity on that ground alone.
accepted.tq: Apply the procedural-versus-substantive distinction to a short constitutional situation.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?
1. Article 245 — Territorial extent of laws
2. Article 246 — Subject-matter of laws under the Seventh Schedule
3. Article 248 — Residuary powers
4. Article 255 — Repugnancy between Union and State laws
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Articles 245, 246 and 248 are correctly matched. Repugnancy is dealt with by Article 254, not Article 255; Article 255 concerns recommendations and previous sanctions as procedural matters.
accepted.tq: Catch the swapped article number in an otherwise familiar constitutional sequence.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the territorial extent of laws, consider the following statements:
1. Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of India.
2. Parliament's law is not invalid merely because it has extra-territorial operation.
3. A State Legislature may ordinarily legislate for the territory of another State without any territorial connection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Parliament may legislate for the whole or any part of India, and an extra-territorial operation does not by itself invalidate parliamentary legislation. A State law requires a sufficient territorial nexus for extra-territorial reach, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Test the Union-State contrast and reject the unrestricted claim about State extra-territorial legislation.
accepted.sec: Territorial extent of laws - Article 245  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which constitutional authority's regulations have the force of Acts of Parliament in the Union Territories of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep?
o: The President
The Inter-State Council
The Administrator appointed by the Supreme Court
The Governor
accepted.x: Regulations made by the President for Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep have the force and effect of an Act of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Identify the competent authority instead of confusing Union Territory administration with State gubernatorial power.
accepted.sec: Territorial extent of laws - Article 245  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about legislative powers in specified tribal or Scheduled Areas is correct?
o: The Governor of every State may repeal any parliamentary Act throughout India
The President has no role in tribal areas of the North-Eastern States
Only the State Legislature may modify parliamentary Acts in Scheduled Areas
The Governor may bar or modify the application of parliamentary Acts in Scheduled Areas
accepted.x: The Governor may bar or modify the application of Acts of Parliament in Scheduled Areas. Special powers also exist for the Governor of Assam in Assam tribal areas and for the President in tribal areas of Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
accepted.tq: Use the territorial exception while rejecting overbroad claims about the Governor's power.
accepted.sec: Territorial extent of laws - Article 245  [other exams]

accepted.s: The doctrine of pith and substance is applied primarily to determine which of the following?
o: The procedure for appointing Governors
The true nature and character of a law when legislative fields overlap
The distribution of seats in the Rajya Sabha
The validity of a constitutional amendment under Article 368
accepted.x: Under the doctrine of pith and substance, the true object and character of a law determine the relevant legislative List. Incidental encroachment on another List is generally ignored.
accepted.tq: Match the doctrine with its precise constitutional problem rather than its incidental effect.
accepted.sec: Doctrine of pith and substance applied to list conflicts - cases

accepted.s: A State law on prohibition incidentally affects a matter in another legislative field, but its true nature is within the State List. Which case is associated with upholding such legislation under the doctrine of pith and substance?
o: State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Prafulla Kumar Mukherjee v. Bank of Commerce
K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa
accepted.x: In State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951), the prohibition law was upheld under the doctrine of pith and substance. The incidental encroachment did not alter its true character.
accepted.tq: Connect the factual subject of a case with the doctrine applied in that case.
accepted.sec: Doctrine of pith and substance applied to list conflicts - cases

accepted.s: Which one of the following expressions correctly represents the doctrine of colourable legislation?
o: The later law always overrides the earlier law
What cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly
A State law is valid only if Parliament approves it
Every law must be interpreted narrowly
accepted.x: The doctrine of colourable legislation is expressed by the maxim that what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly. It is associated with K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa (1953).
accepted.tq: Test the exact maxim associated with a confusable constitutional doctrine.
accepted.sec: Doctrine of pith and substance applied to list conflicts - cases

accepted.s: Which doctrine requires legislative entries to be read together so that each can operate harmoniously?
o: Pith and substance
Harmonious construction
Repugnancy
Colourable legislation
accepted.x: Harmonious construction requires apparently overlapping entries to be interpreted together so that both retain operative effect.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among neighbouring doctrines by their operative principle.
accepted.sec: Doctrine of pith and substance applied to list conflicts - cases

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only subjects in the Union List?
o: Defence, foreign affairs and atomic energy
Police, prisons and sports
Education, forests and social security
Public order, local government and economic planning
accepted.x: Defence, foreign affairs and atomic energy are Union List subjects. Police, prisons, sports, public order and local government are State subjects, while education, forests, social security and economic planning are in the Concurrent List.
accepted.tq: Group subjects by List and eliminate sets containing a neighbouring-list item.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Forests — Concurrent List, Entry 17A
Prisons — State List, Entry 4
Local government — State List, Entry 5
Sports — Concurrent List, Entry 33
accepted.x: Sports is a State List subject under Entry 33, not a Concurrent List subject. Prisons, local government and forests are correctly matched with their respective Lists and entries.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed List classification in a list-entry matching question.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Education is placed in the Concurrent List under Entry 25. It was transferred from the State List by which Constitutional Amendment?
o: 44th Amendment
24th Amendment
42nd Amendment
73rd Amendment
accepted.x: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment transferred education from the State List to the Concurrent List, where it is covered by Entry 25.
accepted.tq: Combine the present List position with the amendment that changed it.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Social security and social insurance — Concurrent List, Entry 23
Economic and social planning — State List, Entry 20
Forests — Union List, Entry 17A
Education — State List, Entry 25
accepted.x: Social security and social insurance are in the Concurrent List under Entry 23. Economic and social planning is Concurrent Entry 20, forests are Concurrent Entry 17A, and education is Concurrent Entry 25.
accepted.tq: Use the List and entry number together to expose deliberate classification swaps.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Coordination and determination of standards in institutions for higher education is covered by which entry?
o: State List Entry 37
Union List Entry 64
Concurrent List Entry 25
Union List Entry 66
accepted.x: Coordination and determination of standards in institutions for higher education is a Union List subject under Entry 66.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Union entries concerning institutions of national importance and higher-education standards.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the entries relating to elections to State Legislatures and elections conducted by the Election Commission?
o: State Entry 37 and Union Entry 72 respectively
Union Entry 37 and State Entry 72 respectively
Concurrent Entry 25 and Union Entry 64 respectively
State Entry 50 and Concurrent Entry 20 respectively
accepted.x: Elections to the State Legislature are covered by State List Entry 37, subject to parliamentary law. Union Entry 72 covers elections conducted by the Election Commission.
accepted.tq: Separate the subject-specific State entry from the Union entry relating to Election Commission elections.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the State List?
o: Higher-education standards — Entry 66
Land — Entry 18
Atomic energy — Entry 6
Organisation of High Courts — Entry 78
accepted.x: Land is a State List subject under Entry 18. Atomic energy, organisation of High Courts and higher-education standards are Union List subjects under Entries 6, 78 and 66 respectively.
accepted.tq: Identify the State entry while eliminating familiar Union List entries.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Police — State List Entry 2
Mineral rights taxation — State List Entry 50
Atomic energy — State List Entry 6
Public order — State List Entry 1
accepted.x: Atomic energy is a Union List subject under Entry 6, not a State List subject. Public order, police and taxes on mineral rights are correctly associated with State List Entries 1, 2 and 50.
accepted.tq: Watch for a wrong List label attached to an otherwise correct entry number.
accepted.sec: Subject → list  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A State Legislature passes a law whose true subject is within the State List, although the law incidentally affects a Union List matter. Which principle would most directly support its validity?
o: Doctrine of colourable legislation
Rule of repugnancy under Article 254
Doctrine of pleasure
Doctrine of pith and substance
accepted.x: The doctrine of pith and substance looks to the true nature and character of the law and disregards incidental encroachment on another legislative field.
accepted.tq: Apply the doctrine to an overlap scenario by focusing on the law's true subject.
accepted.sec: Doctrine of pith and substance applied to list conflicts - cases

accepted.s: Under Article 252, a parliamentary law made on a State subject at the request of two or more States may subsequently be adopted by:
o: Only the States that originally requested it
The President without any State resolution
The Supreme Court through an advisory opinion
Any other State by passing a resolution in its Legislature
accepted.x: Article 252 permits Parliament to legislate for two or more consenting States on a State subject. Any other State may later adopt that law by passing a resolution in its Legislature.
accepted.tq: Test the consent mechanism and the route by which additional States may adopt the law.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With respect to restrictions imposed by a State on inter-State trade, which one of the following is correct?
o: Every restriction is prohibited irrespective of public interest
Parliament can discriminate freely between States during normal conditions
Reasonable restrictions in the public interest may be imposed, but the Bill requires the President's previous sanction
The Governor's previous sanction is sufficient in every case
accepted.x: A State may impose reasonable restrictions on inter-State trade in the public interest, but a Bill for that purpose requires the President's previous sanction. Parliament is also restricted from discriminating between States except in situations of scarcity.
accepted.tq: Combine the substantive test of reasonableness with the procedural requirement of prior sanction.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding parliamentary legislation for implementing international agreements is correct?
o: Only the concerned State Legislature may implement such an agreement
Parliament may make a law for implementing an international treaty or agreement even when the subject would otherwise fall outside its ordinary legislative field
Parliament may legislate only if the subject is already in the Union List
Such legislation is possible only after a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249
accepted.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing international treaties, agreements and conventions, notwithstanding the ordinary distribution of legislative subjects.
accepted.tq: Reject restrictions imported from Article 249 and identify the independent treaty-implementation power.
accepted.sec: Part XI Chapter I - Articles 245-255; Article 255  [APPSC]
